step1_analysis.circuit_type: Differential Reset Switch with Offset Compensation
step1_analysis.description: A switch network designed to reset differential nodes (N1, N2) to a common reference voltage (VRES). It includes a delta-configuration of reset switches (XM1-XM3) and asymmetric dummy switches (XM4-XM7) likely used to compensate for charge injection or to introduce a deliberate offset for the ADC comparators.

t_reset.description: Time required to reset the differential nodes to the reference voltage after the clock goes high.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_on ≈ 1 / (u_n * C_ox * (W/L) * (Vgs - Vth)) ≈ 1 / (270e-6 * 10 * 0.3) ≈ 1.2 kΩ. With a 1pF load, τ = 1.2ns. Settling to 1% takes ~4.6τ ≈ 5.5ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the load capacitance of the T/H or comparator being driven. Estimated for a 1pF test load.

v_inj_cm.description: Common-mode voltage error introduced by charge injection when the reset switches turn off.

sky130_expected.calculation: Q_inj ≈ W * L * C_ox * (Vgs - Vth) / 2 ≈ 2.5um² * 5fF/um² * 0.3V / 2 ≈ 1.8fC. ΔV = Q_inj / C_load ≈ 1.8fC / 1pF = 1.8mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Electrons injected from the NMOS channel into the nodes will slightly lower the common-mode voltage.

v_inj_diff.description: Differential voltage error introduced by asymmetric charge injection, used for offset compensation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Asymmetry between XM5 (NMOS) and XM6 (PMOS) causes unequal charge injection. Difference is roughly proportional to the difference in their channel charges.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The deliberate asymmetry in the dummy switches (NMOS vs PMOS) is designed to create a specific differential offset.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the reset settling time and the common-mode/differential charge injection errors when the clock turns off.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Differential Reset Switch
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u

XM1 VRES PHI2 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N1 PHI2 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N2 PHI2 VRES GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N4 VDD N1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N3 PHI2 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N4 PHI2 N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N3 VDD N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVRES VRES 0 0.9
* 125 MHz clock -> 8ns period
VPHI2 PHI2 0 PULSE(0 1.8 1n 0.1n 0.1n 3.8n 8n)

C1 N1 0 1p
C2 N2 0 1p

* Initial conditions to simulate the nodes needing a reset
.ic v(N1)=1.4 v(N2)=0.4

.control
tran 0.01n 16n uic

* Measure reset time (settling to within ~10mV of VRES)
meas tran t_reset_n1 trig v(PHI2) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(N1) val=0.91 fall=1
meas tran t_reset_n2 trig v(PHI2) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(N2) val=0.89 rise=1

* Measure voltages after switches turn off (at 7ns, before next rising edge)
meas tran v_n1_final find v(N1) at=7n
meas tran v_n2_final find v(N2) at=7n

* Calculate charge injection errors
let v_inj_cm = ((v_n1_final + v_n2_final) / 2) - 0.9
let v_inj_diff = v_n1_final - v_n2_final

print t_reset_n1 t_reset_n2 v_inj_cm v_inj_diff
quit
.endc
